title: The memory that grows forever
blurb: The draft leaves the session buffer untrimmed, unexpired and shared across tenants.
prompt: A tenant reported latency that grows through long sessions, and two tenants with colliding session ids saw each other in the buffer. The model-generated draft pushes turns onto a Redis list with no trim and no TTL and builds keys from the session id alone. Review it, fix it, and prove the buffer is bounded, expiring and tenant-scoped.
aiNote: The draft pushes each turn onto an unbounded Redis list with no TTL and no trim, builds the key without the tenant prefix so colliding session ids share a buffer, and appends without an idempotency key so a client retry writes the same turn twice.
testIdea: Append 60 turns and assert the list holds 50; replay one append with the same Idempotency-Key and assert a single turn; read two tenants with the same session id and assert their buffers are disjoint.
followUps: How would you summarize older turns without blocking the append path?
Should the summary live in Redis or in durable storage, and why?
What breaks if two instances append to one session while the buffer is trimmed?
